plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet mandate.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown. Returns will likely be modest, but with reduced risk.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration and meet mandate.
Buy TECL for 4% of the book, adding a strong tech setup.
Buy NVDU for 4% of the book, adding another strong tech setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, reducing overall leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leveraged ETF exposure and concentration, while adding quality tech setups. Expect moderate returns with controlled risk.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet mandate.
Sell SOXL and SPAL as they are below their stops, reallocating capital.
Buy TECL for 6% of the book, adding a strong leveraged tech setup.
Buy NVDU for 6% of the book, adding a strong tech setup.
Buy NVDA for 6% of the book, adding another strong tech setup.
This plan leans into high-scoring setups and uses leverage strategically.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It utilizes strong scanner setups and maintains leverage, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Add QQQI to 30% of the book, increasing income exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet mandate.
Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
Buy ORCL for 5% of the book, adding a quality name for potential yield.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes income and broad index exposure, cutting high-beta names and leverage. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
